title: Contrix Realm Join Candidate
description: Time-bounded routing hint for submitting Realm join, invite-accept, knock, or restricted-join material through a qualified Realm service. This object is not membership authorization and is distinct from member_delivery_binding.

realm_id.description: Realm this candidate is bound to. Verifiers MUST reject a candidate used for any other Realm.

service_did.description: Service DID that can receive or relay join-side submissions for this Realm.

service_type.description: Service class. principal_server is the normal candidate; sync_node and anchorer are allowed only when Realm policy authorizes them to receive join-side submissions.

role.description: Routing role within the Realm candidate set. This is a hint for ordering and diagnostics, not an authorization grant.

endpoint.description: Optional endpoint hint. Callers MUST re-resolve the service DID document before transport and MUST NOT treat this field as authority.

operations.description: Endpoint-callable operation ids available at this candidate. Join-side routing requires cx.events.submit.

join_methods.description: Join-side flows this candidate claims to support for this requester and Realm.

priority.description: Lower values are preferred. Ties are broken deterministically by service_did.

source.description: Where this routing hint came from. Receivers still validate against current Realm policy and service DID documents.

source_refs.description: Realm or directory source events that justify this candidate, such as discovery, service-binding, or sync endpoint state.

frontier_ref.description: Optional digest of the candidate service's advertised Realm frontier at as_of; used only to detect stale hints.

as_of.description: Time when the issuer observed or refreshed this candidate.

expires_at.description: Time after which clients MUST NOT use this candidate without re-resolving the Realm.

proofs.description: Optional proof set binding realm_id, service_did, role, operations, join_methods, as_of, and expires_at. Required when the candidate is carried outside a freshly resolved Directory response.
